newsitem.title: USA: U.S. deficit expected to decline to about $36 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. deficit expected to decline to about $36 bln.

text.p: President Clinton is expected to announce Wednesday that the U.S. budget deficit for the current fiscal year has declined further to about $36 billion, an administration official said.

The new estimate of a further dramatic decline in deficit spending, evidence of a booming economy and surging tax revenues, came only a week after White House budget director Franklin Raines said the budget deficit for fiscal 1997 would be below $50 billion.
An administration official, who asked to remain unidentified, said the new estimate was about $36 billion.
Clinton was expected to announce the new estimate at a 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) news conference and promote it as further evidence that his economic plan was working.
The new estimate came a day after Clinton signed legislation intended to balance the federal budget by 2002 while at the same time giving Americans a big tax cut.
The United States has not posted a budget surplus since 1969.
